questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 1.3
questions.subject: CO & Architecture
questions.questionHtml:
In a vectored interrupt:

  1. The branch address is assigned to a fixed location in memory

  2. The interrupting source supplies the branch information to the processor through an interrupt vector

  3. The branch address is obtained from a register in the processor

  4. None of the above

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 1.4
questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.questionHtml:
In the following Pascal program segment, what is the value of X after the execution of the program segment?

X := -10; Y := 20;
If X > Y then if X < 0 then X := abs(X) else X := 2*X;
  1. $10$
  2. $-20$
  3. $-10$
  4. None

questions.questionHtml:

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 1.9 , ISRO2017-13
questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.questionHtml:
In some programming language, an identifier is permitted to be a letter followed by any number of letters or digits. If $L$ and $D$ denote the sets of letters and digits respectively, which of the following expressions defines an identifier?

  1. $(L + D)^+$
  2. $(L.D)^*$
  3. $L(L + D)^*$
  4. $L(L.D)^*$

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 1.10
questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.questionHtml:
Consider a grammar with the following productions

[latex]S \rightarrow a \alpha b \mid b \alpha c \mid aB[/latex]

[latex]S \rightarrow \alpha S\mid b[/latex]

[latex]S \rightarrow \alpha b b\mid ab[/latex]

[latex]S \alpha \rightarrow bd b\mid b[/latex]

The above grammar is:

  1. Context free

  2. Regular

  3. Context sensitive

  4. LR(k)

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 2.2

questions.questionHtml:

  2. $11$ address, $8$ data lines
  3. $12$ address, $16$ data lines
  4. $12$ address, $12$ data lines

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 2.3
questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.questionHtml:
Assume that $X$ and $Y$ are non-zero positive integers. What does the following Pascal program segment do?

while X <> Y do
if  X > Y then
    X := X - Y
else
    Y := Y - X;
write(X);

  1. Computes the LCM of two numbers

  2. Divides the larger number by the smaller number

  3. Computes the GCD of two numbers

  4. None of the above

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 2.4
questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.questionHtml:
What is the value of $X$ printed by the following program?

program COMPUTE (input, output);
var X:integer;
procedure FIND (X:real);
    begin
        X:=sqrt(X);
    end;
begin
    X:=2
    FIND(X);
    writeln(X);
end.
  1. $2$
  2. $\sqrt{2}$
  3. Run time error
  4. None of the above

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 2.5
questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.questionHtml:

$\overline{A} + AB =0, AB=AC, AB+A\overline{C}+CD=\overline{C}D$

  1. $A=1, B=0, C=0, D=1$

  2. $A=1, B=1, C=0, D=0$

  3. $A=1, B=0, C=1, D=1$

  4. $A=1, B=0, C=0, D=0$

questions.title: GATE CSE 1995 | Question: 2.9
questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.questionHtml:
A language with string manipulation facilities uses the following operations

head(s): first character of a string
tail(s): all but exclude the first character of a string
concat(s1, s2): s1s2

For the string "$acbc$" what will be the output of

concat(head(s), head(tail(tail(s))))
  1. $ac$
  2. $bc$
  3. $ab$
  4. $cc$
